note: Original MCQs written for this bot plus the free-tier MCQs of pharma3sem.publicvm.com. Correct answer is "correct"; options are shuffled at send time.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The resonance energy of benzene obtained from heats of hydrogenation is about:
questions.explain: Expected 85.8 (3 x 28.6) minus observed 49.8 = about 36 kcal/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In nitration of benzene, the actual electrophile is:
questions.explain: Conc. H2SO4 protonates HNO3, which loses water to form the nitronium ion NO2+.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which compound does NOT undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction?
questions.explain: -NO2 strongly deactivates the ring; nitrobenzene is even used as a solvent for FC reactions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Gammexane (lindane) is:
questions.explain: Gamma-BHC (C6H6Cl6) is the active insecticidal isomer, used for scabies and lice.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Number of pi electrons in the cyclopentadienyl anion and its nature is:
questions.explain: Planar, cyclic, conjugated with 6 pi electrons (n = 1).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Phenol on treatment with CHCl3 and aqueous NaOH followed by acidification gives:
questions.explain: Reimer-Tiemann reaction; the electrophile is dichlorocarbene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Arrange in decreasing order of basicity: (I) aniline, (II) p-toluidine, (III) p-nitroaniline, (IV) methylamine
questions.explain: Alkylamine most basic; EDG at para raises and NO2 lowers aniline's basicity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Fluorobenzene is best prepared from benzenediazonium salt by:
questions.explain: The diazonium fluoroborate (from HBF4) decomposes on heating to ArF.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which test is given by phenol with NaNO2 and conc. H2SO4 (green/blue colour, red on dilution)?
questions.explain: Liebermann's test for phenols.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reichert-Meissl value is defined for how much fat?
questions.explain: RM value: ml of 0.1 N alkali for volatile water-soluble acids from 5 g fat.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A fat with high saponification value contains mainly:
questions.explain: SV is inversely proportional to mean molecular weight.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ester value is equal to:
questions.explain: Esters = total saponifiable minus free acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which antioxidant is NOT used to prevent rancidity of oils?
questions.explain: BHA, BHT and tocopherol are antioxidants; NaCl is not.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which oil has the highest iodine value?
questions.explain: Linseed oil is rich in linolenic acid, a drying oil (IV above 170).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Catalytic air oxidation of naphthalene over V2O5 gives:
questions.explain: One ring is oxidised away leaving phthalic anhydride.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus is present in:
questions.explain: It is the steroid nucleus (cholesterol, hormones, cardiac glycosides).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reduction of naphthalene with sodium and isoamyl alcohol gives:
questions.explain: Na/isoamyl alcohol (higher temp) gives 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene; Na/ethanol gives 1,4-dihydro.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Baeyer's strain theory predicted the most stable ring to be:
questions.explain: Cyclopentane has the smallest deviation (0 deg 44') for a planar ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cyclopropane reacts with HBr to give:
questions.explain: HBr opens the strained ring giving n-propyl bromide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which statement about cyclohexane is correct?
questions.correct: Chair form has all bonds staggered
wrong: It is planar with 120 deg angles
Boat form is more stable than chair
questions.explain: Chair: staggered bonds, no angle or torsional strain; 6 axial and 6 equatorial H.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: According to the pharmacopoeia, a drug that needs 30 to 100 parts of solvent to dissolve 1 part is described as:
questions.explain: Sparingly soluble = 30-100 parts; soluble = 10-30; slightly soluble = 100-1000.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The Hildebrand solubility parameter is the square root of:
questions.explain: δ = [(ΔHv - RT)/V]^1/2 = (cohesive energy density)^1/2.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: A minimum-boiling azeotrope is formed by systems showing:
questions.explain: Positive deviation gives a vapour pressure maximum and hence a boiling point minimum (e.g. ethanol-water).

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Which system shows both upper and lower critical solution temperatures?
questions.explain: Nicotine-water gives a closed-loop miscibility curve.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The latent heat of vaporization of water at 100°C is about:
questions.explain: About 540 cal/g (2257 J/g); 80 cal/g is the latent heat of fusion of ice.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The critical temperature of water is about:
questions.explain: Water's critical point is about 374°C and 218 atm (647 K is the same temperature in kelvin, not °C).

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Polymorphs that can convert reversibly into each other at a transition temperature are:
questions.explain: Enantiotropic forms interconvert reversibly (e.g. sulfur); monotropic forms change only one way.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The dipole moment of carbon dioxide is zero because it is:
questions.explain: The two C=O bond dipoles are equal and opposite in the linear molecule and cancel.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The surface tension of water at 20°C is about:
questions.explain: Water ≈ 72.8 dyne/cm (mN/m) at 20°C.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Which method is used to measure interfacial tension as well as surface tension?
questions.explain: The du Noüy ring can be pulled through the interface of two liquids; capillary rise cannot measure interfacial tension.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: According to Griffin's scale, w/o emulsifying agents have HLB values of about:
questions.explain: 3-6 w/o emulsifiers; 8-18 o/w emulsifiers; 15-18 solubilisers.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: For a positively adsorbed surfactant, the Gibbs adsorption equation shows that:
questions.explain: Γ = -(c/RT)(dγ/dc); positive Γ requires surface tension to fall with concentration.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: β-cyclodextrin contains how many glucose units?
questions.explain: α = 6, β = 7, γ = 8 glucose units.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Urea and deoxycholic acid form which type of inclusion compound?
questions.explain: They crystallise with long channels that hold guest molecules.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: In the Scatchard plot (r/Df vs r), the slope equals:
questions.explain: r/Df = nK - rK; slope -K, x-intercept n.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Absorption of tetracycline is reduced by milk and antacids because of:
questions.correct: Chelation with Ca, Mg and Al ions
questions.explain: Tetracyclines form poorly absorbed chelates with polyvalent metal ions.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Maximum buffer capacity of a buffer of total concentration C is:
questions.explain: βmax = 2.303 C/4 = 0.576 C at pH = pKa.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The main buffer system of blood plasma is:
questions.explain: H2CO3/HCO3- is the principal plasma buffer.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The Liso value for uni-univalent electrolytes such as NaCl is about:
questions.explain: Liso ≈ 1.9 non-electrolytes, 2.0 weak electrolytes, 3.4 uni-univalent, 4.3 uni-divalent.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The glass electrode suffers from alkaline (sodium) error at:
questions.explain: At high pH and high Na+ the glass responds to sodium ions and reads pH too low.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Ribosomes found in the cytoplasm of bacteria are of which type?
questions.explain: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes (50S + 30S); eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: In which phase of the growth curve is the generation time shortest and constant?
questions.explain: Cells divide at a constant maximum rate in the log (exponential) phase.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Which microscope is the method of choice for demonstrating Treponema pallidum in a fresh specimen?
questions.explain: Treponema is too thin for bright field; dark field shows it as bright spirals on a dark background.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Which method gives the viable count of bacteria?
questions.explain: Only plate counts (CFU) measure living cells; the others count live and dead cells.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: In Gram staining, the step that differentiates Gram-positive from Gram-negative bacteria is:
questions.explain: Decolouriser removes the crystal violet-iodine complex only from Gram-negative cells.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The biological indicator used to monitor moist heat sterilization is spores of:
questions.explain: G. stearothermophilus spores are highly resistant to moist heat.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The Bowie-Dick test is used to check:
questions.correct: Air removal and steam penetration in an autoclave
questions.explain: Bowie-Dick test pack shows uniform colour change only if air is removed properly.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Ethylene oxide kills microorganisms mainly by:
questions.correct: Alkylation of proteins and nucleic acids
questions.explain: EtO is an alkylating agent acting on -SH, -NH2, -OH and -COOH groups.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The cell wall of fungi is mainly composed of:
questions.explain: Fungal walls contain chitin and glucans; peptidoglycan is bacterial.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Influenza virus for vaccine production is traditionally grown in the:
questions.explain: Influenza virus is grown in the allantoic cavity of embryonated hen's eggs.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: A disinfectant with a high concentration exponent (e.g. phenol, n = 6) means:
wrong: It is unaffected by organic matter
Dilution has little effect on activity
questions.explain: Activity falls by 2^n when concentration is halved; for n = 6 that is 64-fold.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The membrane pore size used in the membrane filtration method of sterility testing is:
questions.explain: Pharmacopoeias specify a membrane of nominal pore size not greater than 0.45 µm for the sterility test.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: A HEPA filter removes at least what percentage of 0.3 µm particles?
questions.explain: HEPA filters are rated at 99.97% efficiency for 0.3 µm particles.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The recommended air velocity of unidirectional airflow in a Grade A zone (EU GMP guidance) is about:
questions.explain: EU GMP Annex 1 guidance value is 0.36-0.54 m/s at the working position.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Vitamin B12 is assayed microbiologically using:
questions.explain: L. leichmannii requires B12 for growth; its growth is proportional to B12 content.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The main advantage of the turbidimetric assay over the cylinder-plate method is:
questions.explain: Turbidimetric assays need only about 3-4 h incubation versus 16-18 h for plates.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Benzoic acid is an effective preservative only at acidic pH because:
questions.correct: Only its unionised form is antimicrobial
questions.explain: Weak acid preservatives act in the unionised form, which predominates below their pKa (about 4.2).

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Which organism is NOT among the standard challenge organisms in the preservative efficacy test?
questions.explain: Challenge organisms are S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, E. coli (oral), C. albicans and A. brasiliensis; C. sporogenes is used in sterility test controls.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Which is a continuous (established) cell line widely used for recombinant protein production?
questions.explain: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells are immortal and used for monoclonal antibodies and other biologics.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Animal cell cultures are commonly incubated in an atmosphere containing:
questions.explain: 5% CO2 maintains the bicarbonate-buffered pH of the medium at about 7.2-7.4.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Reynolds number is the ratio of:
questions.explain: Re = Duρ/μ = inertial force / viscous force; it is dimensionless.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: The coefficient of discharge of a venturimeter is about:
questions.explain: Venturimeter has very little loss (Cd ≈ 0.98); an orifice meter has Cd ≈ 0.61 due to vena contracta and eddies.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Kick's law of size reduction is most applicable to:
questions.explain: Kick's law (energy ∝ size reduction ratio) fits coarse crushing; Rittinger's law fits fine grinding.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: For efficient grinding, a ball mill should be operated at:
questions.correct: About one-half to three-fourth of critical speed
wrong: Less than one-tenth of critical speed
questions.explain: At critical speed balls centrifuge with the wall; at too low speed they only roll. Cascading at 50-75% of critical speed gives maximum impact.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: As per IP, a 'very fine powder' is one in which all particles pass through sieve number:
questions.explain: IP grades: coarse 10/44, moderately coarse 22/60, moderately fine 44/85, fine 85, very fine 120.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Fourier's law is the basic law of heat transfer by:
questions.explain: dQ/dθ = -kA dt/dx describes conduction through a solid.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Economy of an evaporator is defined as:
questions.correct: Kg of water evaporated per kg of steam supplied
wrong: Kg of steam used per hour
Heat transfer area per kg of feed
questions.explain: Economy = kg vapour produced / kg steam fed.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Backward feeding in a multiple effect evaporator is preferred when:
questions.correct: Feed is cold and the concentrate is viscous
wrong: Feed is hot and concentrate is thermolabile
questions.explain: In backward feed the most concentrated (viscous) liquid is in the hottest first effect, where viscosity is lowest.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Steam distillation is based on the principle that:
questions.correct: Immiscible liquids boil when the sum of their vapour pressures equals atmospheric pressure
wrong: Molecules travel less than mean free path
questions.explain: Each immiscible liquid exerts its own vapour pressure, so the mixture boils below 100 °C.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Flash distillation is also known as:
questions.explain: Vapour and liquid formed by sudden pressure release are in equilibrium and are separated.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: The second falling rate period of drying is controlled by:
questions.correct: Movement of moisture from inside to the surface (diffusion/capillary)
questions.explain: In this period internal moisture movement, not external conditions, limits the rate.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: The triple point of water is at:
questions.explain: Below 4.58 mm Hg ice sublimes directly without melting.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Tumbling blenders such as double cone and V-blender mix powders mainly by:
questions.explain: Random movement of individual particles over freshly formed surfaces during tumbling is diffusive mixing.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: A propeller mixer mainly produces:
questions.explain: Propellers move liquid parallel to the shaft (up and down), suitable for low-viscosity liquids.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: According to Poiseuille's equation, flow rate through a capillary is proportional to:
questions.explain: dV/dt = πr⁴ΔP / 8ηL; doubling pore radius increases flow 16 times.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: The pore size of a membrane filter used for sterile filtration is:
questions.explain: 0.22 µm (or 0.2 µm) membranes retain bacteria; 0.45 µm is used for clarification.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: A rotary drum filter is a:
questions.explain: The drum rotates continuously through filtration, washing, drying and discharge zones under vacuum.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Relative centrifugal force (RCF) in terms of radius r (cm) and speed N (rpm) is:
questions.explain: RCF = ω²r/g = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ r N²; it increases with the square of speed.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: In cathodic protection by the sacrificial anode method, the anode commonly used is:
questions.explain: A more active metal (Zn, Mg) corrodes in place of the protected steel.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Pitting corrosion of stainless steel is mainly promoted by:
questions.explain: Chlorides break down the passive film at local points, forming deep pits.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which of the following is an official dosage form meant for application to the eye?
questions.explain: Ophthalmic ointments are sterile semisolids for the eye; liniments and paints are for skin.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Hard gelatin capsule size with the LARGEST capacity among these is:
questions.explain: Capsule sizes run 000 (largest) to 5 (smallest).

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Suppository base that melts at body temperature is:
questions.explain: Cocoa butter melts around 30–35 °C; PEG and glycero-gelatin dissolve in body fluids instead.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Displacement value is used in the preparation of:
questions.explain: It tells how many grams of base one gram of drug displaces in a suppository mould.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which is an example of a hydrocarbon (oleaginous) ointment base?
questions.explain: Hydrocarbon bases like soft paraffin are occlusive and water-insoluble.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: A liquid oral preparation containing a high concentration of sucrose (about 66.7% w/w) is a:
questions.explain: Simple Syrup IP contains 66.7% w/w sucrose.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Elixirs are best described as:
questions.correct: Clear, sweetened hydroalcoholic liquids for oral use
questions.explain: Elixirs are clear, pleasantly flavoured hydro-alcoholic solutions.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which test is NOT an official quality control test for uncoated tablets?
questions.explain: Viscosity is for liquids; tablets get weight variation, disintegration, friability, hardness etc.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Acceptable friability limit for most conventional compressed tablets is a weight loss of NOT more than:
questions.explain: Pharmacopoeial friability limit is ≤1% weight loss.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Lubricant commonly used in tablet manufacture is:
questions.explain: Magnesium stearate reduces die-wall friction; starch paste is a binder, lactose a diluent.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which excipient is mainly used as a tablet disintegrant?
questions.explain: Sodium starch glycolate is a superdisintegrant that swells in water.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Capping and lamination of tablets are mainly due to:
questions.explain: Entrapped air and too many fines cause the tablet top to split off (capping) or layer (lamination).

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Mottling in tablets refers to:
questions.explain: Mottling = uneven colour on the tablet surface.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: The process of applying a sugar coat in several steps begins with:
questions.explain: Sugar coating order: sealing → subcoating → smoothing → colouring → polishing → printing.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Enteric coating is designed to:
questions.correct: Resist gastric fluid and dissolve in the intestine
questions.explain: Enteric polymers (e.g. CAP) stay intact at stomach pH and dissolve at intestinal pH.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Cellulose acetate phthalate is used as:
questions.explain: CAP is a classic enteric coating material.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which is a glidant used in tablet formulation?
questions.explain: Colloidal silica (Aerosil) improves powder flow.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Water for Injection is mainly prepared by:
questions.explain: WFI is made by distillation (or RO with suitable treatment) and must be pyrogen-free.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Pyrogens in parenterals are mainly:
questions.explain: Pyrogens are mostly lipopolysaccharide endotoxins from gram-negative bacteria.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: The LAL test detects:
questions.explain: Limulus Amebocyte Lysate gels in the presence of endotoxin.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Isotonic sodium chloride solution has a concentration of about:
questions.explain: Normal saline 0.9% w/v is isotonic with blood.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Freezing point of blood and lachrymal fluid is about:
questions.explain: Isotonic solutions show a freezing point depression of 0.52 °C.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which is a primary emulsifier of natural origin?
questions.explain: Acacia (gum arabic) is a natural hydrophilic colloid emulsifier.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: The 'dry gum' method of emulsion preparation uses oil : water : gum ratio for fixed oils of:
questions.explain: Continental (dry gum) method for fixed oils uses 4 parts oil, 2 water, 1 gum.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Creaming of an emulsion is:
questions.explain: Creaming is reversible by shaking; cracking (coalescence) is irreversible.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Cracking of an emulsion means:
questions.explain: Cracking is the irreversible breaking of the emulsion.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Flocculated suspensions characteristically:
questions.correct: Form a loose sediment that redisperses easily
wrong: Settle very slowly as individual particles
questions.explain: Flocs settle fast but give a fluffy, easily redispersible sediment.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Caking in suspensions is associated with:
questions.explain: Deflocculated particles settle slowly but pack into a hard, non-redispersible cake.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which suspending agent is a clay?
questions.explain: Bentonite is a colloidal clay; the others are cellulose or natural gums.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Lyophilization is also called:
questions.explain: Lyophilization removes water by sublimation from the frozen state.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Prescription abbreviation 'b.i.d.' means:
questions.explain: b.i.d. = bis in die (twice daily); t.i.d. thrice; h.s. at bedtime; a.c. before meals.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Prescription abbreviation 'a.c.' means:
questions.explain: a.c. = ante cibum (before food); p.c. = after food.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Young's formula for child dose is:
questions.explain: Young's rule = Age ÷ (Age + 12) × adult dose.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Clark's rule calculates child dose from:
questions.explain: Clark's rule = weight (lb)/150 × adult dose.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Dilling's formula for child dose uses:
questions.explain: Dilling's rule = Age ÷ 20 × adult dose.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Incompatibility seen as a visible change like precipitation or colour change is called:
questions.explain: Visible changes are physical or chemical incompatibilities; therapeutic ones relate to effects.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Effervescent granules contain citric acid, tartaric acid and:
questions.explain: The acids react with sodium bicarbonate in water to release CO2.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Which type of glass is used for most aqueous parenteral containers needing best chemical resistance?
questions.explain: Type I borosilicate glass has the highest hydrolytic resistance.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Moist heat sterilization in an autoclave is commonly done at:
questions.explain: Standard autoclave cycle: 121 °C, 15 psi, 15 minutes.

questions.subject: pharmaceutics
questions.q: Dry heat sterilization (hot air oven) typical cycle is:
questions.explain: Hot air oven: 160 °C for 2 h (or 170 °C for 1 h).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Number of π electrons in benzene is:
questions.explain: Benzene has three C=C double bonds = 6 π electrons, satisfying 4n+2 with n=1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hybridization of each carbon atom in benzene is:
questions.explain: Each ring carbon is sp2 with one unhybridized p orbital in the π cloud.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: C–C bond length in benzene is about:
questions.explain: All six bonds are equal at ~1.39 Å, between single (1.54) and double (1.34).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The electrophile in nitration of benzene is:
questions.explain: HNO3 + H2SO4 generate NO2+, which attacks the ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Friedel–Crafts alkylation uses which catalyst?
questions.explain: Lewis acid AlCl3 generates the carbocation electrophile from alkyl halide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which group is a meta director?
questions.explain: Electron-withdrawing –NO2 deactivates the ring and directs meta.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Halogens on benzene are:
questions.explain: Halogens withdraw by induction (deactivate) but donate by resonance (o/p).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the most acidic?
questions.explain: –NO2 stabilizes the phenoxide ion by resonance, increasing acidity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
questions.explain: The negative charge of phenoxide delocalizes into the ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reaction of phenol with CHCl3 and NaOH giving salicylaldehyde is:
questions.explain: Reimer–Tiemann adds –CHO ortho via dichlorocarbene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Kolbe–Schmitt reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO2 gives:
questions.explain: Sodium phenoxide + CO2 (pressure, heat) → salicylic acid, precursor of aspirin.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the strongest base?
questions.explain: Alkyl group pushes electrons to N; in aniline the lone pair is delocalized into the ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because:
questions.correct: Its lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring
wrong: It is more soluble in water
questions.explain: Resonance reduces lone-pair availability on nitrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzene diazonium chloride is prepared from aniline using:
questions.explain: Diazotization needs cold nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Conversion of diazonium salt to chlorobenzene using CuCl is:
questions.explain: Sandmeyer uses Cu(I) salts to replace –N2+ by Cl, Br or CN.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzoic acid is more acidic than acetic acid mainly due to:
questions.explain: pKa benzoic ≈ 4.2 vs acetic ≈ 4.76; the phenyl group stabilizes the carboxylate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Saponification value of a fat is the mg of KOH required to saponify:
questions.explain: Higher saponification value means shorter average fatty acid chain.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Iodine value of an oil indicates its:
questions.explain: Iodine value = g of iodine absorbed by 100 g oil; more double bonds = higher value.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Acid value of a fat measures:
questions.explain: Acid value = mg KOH to neutralize free fatty acids in 1 g fat.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Rancidity of fats is mainly due to:
questions.explain: Oxidative and hydrolytic rancidity produce off-odour aldehydes and acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reichert–Meissl value measures:
questions.explain: It is high for butter, used to detect adulteration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Naphthalene contains how many fused benzene rings?
questions.explain: Naphthalene = two fused rings; anthracene and phenanthrene have three.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which polynuclear hydrocarbon is a known carcinogen?
questions.explain: Benzo[a]pyrene from smoke and tar is a potent carcinogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Baeyer strain theory explains stability of:
questions.explain: Baeyer related angle strain to deviation from 109.5° in planar rings.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Most stable conformation of cyclohexane is:
questions.explain: The chair form has no angle strain and staggered C–H bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzaldehyde with conc. NaOH undergoes which reaction (no α-hydrogen)?
questions.explain: Aldehydes without α-H disproportionate to alcohol + carboxylate (Cannizzaro).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cyclopropane reacts with H2/Ni to give:
questions.explain: Its high ring strain allows ring opening by hydrogenation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sachse–Mohr theory proposed that larger rings are:
questions.explain: Rings like cyclohexane pucker into strain-free shapes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Picric acid is chemically:
questions.explain: Three –NO2 groups make picric acid strongly acidic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Oxidation of toluene with KMnO4 gives:
questions.explain: Alkaline KMnO4 oxidizes the side chain to –COOH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aspirin is synthesized by acetylation of:
questions.explain: Salicylic acid + acetic anhydride → acetylsalicylic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Paracetamol is chemically:
questions.explain: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) = 4-hydroxyacetanilide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Huckel aromatic among these is:
questions.explain: The anion has 6 π electrons in a planar ring; cyclobutadiene is antiaromatic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Clemmensen reduction converts a ketone to an alkane using:
questions.explain: Clemmensen = zinc amalgam + HCl; Wolff–Kishner uses hydrazine/base.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sulphonation of benzene uses:
questions.explain: SO3 in oleum is the electrophile; the reaction is reversible.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Anthracene and phenanthrene are:
questions.explain: Both are three-ring PAHs, C14H10, differing in ring fusion (linear vs angular).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is used in the synthesis of DDT along with chloral?
questions.explain: DDT forms from chlorobenzene + chloral in H2SO4.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Bromination of phenol with bromine water gives:
questions.explain: –OH strongly activates; all ortho/para positions brominate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Nitrobenzene reduced with Sn/HCl gives:
questions.explain: Acidic metal reduction converts –NO2 to –NH2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogenation of oils (as in vanaspati) mainly:
questions.correct: Converts unsaturated fats to saturated, raising melting point
questions.explain: H2 with Ni adds across C=C bonds, hardening the oil.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation for a weak acid is:
questions.explain: For a weak acid buffer, pH = pKa + log [A−]/[HA].

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: A buffer has maximum buffer capacity when:
questions.explain: Capacity peaks when [salt] = [acid], i.e. pH = pKa.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Surface tension is expressed in:
questions.explain: Surface tension is force per unit length.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Surface tension of a liquid generally ____ with rise in temperature.
questions.explain: Higher temperature weakens intermolecular cohesion.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Instrument used to measure surface tension by ring method:
questions.explain: The du Noüy ring tensiometer measures force to pull a ring from the surface.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: HLB value range for o/w emulsifying agents is about:
questions.explain: Griffin scale: o/w emulsifiers ~8–18; w/o ~3–6.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: HLB range typical of antifoaming agents is:
questions.explain: Antifoams have very low HLB (1–3); solubilizers 15–18.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Critical micelle concentration (CMC) is the concentration at which:
questions.explain: Above CMC, added surfactant forms micelles and surface tension stays nearly constant.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Spreading coefficient S must be ____ for a liquid to spread on another.
questions.explain: S = γ(sub) − (γ(liquid) + γ(interface)); spreading occurs when S > 0.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The Gibbs adsorption equation relates surface excess to:
questions.correct: Change in surface tension with concentration
questions.explain: Γ = −(c/RT)(dγ/dc).

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Freundlich adsorption isotherm is:
questions.explain: Freundlich: amount adsorbed per gram rises as a fractional power of pressure/concentration.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Langmuir adsorption assumes:
questions.explain: Langmuir model: one layer, identical sites, no interaction.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Partition coefficient is the ratio of drug concentrations in:
questions.correct: Oil phase to aqueous phase at equilibrium
questions.explain: K = C(oil)/C(water); higher K = more lipophilic.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Phase rule is expressed as:
questions.explain: Gibbs phase rule: degrees of freedom = components − phases + 2.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: At the triple point of water, degrees of freedom are:
questions.explain: F = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0; it is invariant.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Phenol–water system is an example of:
questions.correct: Partially miscible liquids with upper consolute temperature
questions.explain: Phenol and water become fully miscible above ~66.8 °C.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Nicotine–water system shows:
questions.correct: Both upper and lower consolute temperatures
questions.explain: Nicotine–water forms a closed solubility loop.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Triethylamine–water system shows a:
questions.explain: Triethylamine and water are miscible below about 18.5 °C.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Colligative properties depend on:
questions.explain: Vapour pressure lowering, BP elevation, FP depression and osmotic pressure depend on particle count.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Raoult's law states that partial vapour pressure of a component equals:
questions.correct: Its mole fraction × vapour pressure of pure component
questions.explain: p(A) = x(A) × p°(A) for an ideal solution.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Solutions showing large positive deviation from Raoult's law can form:
questions.explain: Ethanol–water (positive deviation) gives a minimum boiling azeotrope.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Polymorphs of a drug differ in:
questions.correct: Crystal structure, solubility and melting point
questions.explain: Same molecule, different crystal packing; metastable forms dissolve faster.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Which polymorph of chloramphenicol palmitate is therapeutically more active?
questions.explain: Metastable form B dissolves faster and gives higher blood levels.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Amorphous forms of drugs, compared with crystalline forms, usually have:
questions.explain: No lattice energy to overcome, so they dissolve faster.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Liquid crystals that respond to temperature are called:
questions.explain: Thermotropic change with temperature; lyotropic with solvent concentration.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Smectic liquid crystals have molecules arranged in:
questions.explain: Smectic = layered; nematic = parallel without layers; cholesteric = twisted.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Dielectric constant of water at 25 °C is about:
questions.explain: Water's high dielectric constant (~78.5) makes it a good polar solvent.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Refractive index is measured with:
questions.explain: Abbe refractometer measures refractive index; polarimeter measures optical rotation.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Optical rotation is measured with a:
questions.explain: Polarimeter measures rotation of plane-polarized light by chiral molecules.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Dipole moment is expressed in:
questions.explain: 1 Debye = 10⁻¹⁸ esu·cm.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Hydrogen bonding is responsible for the:
questions.correct: High boiling point of water compared with H2S
questions.explain: Water boils at 100 °C vs H2S at about −60 °C because water molecules H-bond.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Solubility of most solids in water ____ with temperature (endothermic dissolution).
questions.explain: Endothermic dissolution is favoured by heat (Le Chatelier).

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Cosolvency means:
questions.correct: Increasing solubility of a drug by adding a water-miscible solvent
questions.explain: E.g. ethanol, propylene glycol or glycerin added to water to dissolve a poorly soluble drug.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Hydrotropy is solubilisation using:
questions.correct: High concentrations of salts like sodium benzoate
questions.explain: Hydrotropes (e.g. sodium benzoate, urea) increase aqueous solubility at high concentration.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: pH of a solution with [H+] = 1 × 10⁻⁴ M is:
questions.explain: pH = −log[H+] = 4.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: The common ion effect generally ____ the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt.
questions.explain: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium toward the solid.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Interfacial tension between water and mineral oil compared to surface tension of water is:
questions.explain: Interfacial tensions are usually lower than surface tension of the more polar liquid.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Contact angle of 0° means:
questions.explain: θ = 0° = liquid spreads fully; θ = 180° = no wetting.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Ionisation of a weak acid drug is greater at:
questions.explain: Above pKa the ionized (A−) form predominates.

questions.subject: physpharm
questions.q: Eutectic mixture example used in topical anaesthesia (EMLA) contains:
questions.explain: EMLA = Eutectic Mixture of Local Anaesthetics (lidocaine + prilocaine).

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Father of microbiology is generally considered:
questions.explain: Leeuwenhoek first observed microbes with his simple microscope (17th century).

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Germ theory of disease and Koch's postulates were given by:
questions.explain: Koch's postulates link a specific microbe to a specific disease.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Pasteurization was developed by:
questions.explain: Pasteur showed heating kills spoilage microbes in wine and milk.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Gram-positive bacteria appear ____ after Gram staining.
questions.explain: Thick peptidoglycan retains crystal violet–iodine complex.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Mordant used in Gram staining is:
questions.explain: Iodine fixes crystal violet; alcohol decolourizes; safranin counterstains.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Counterstain in Gram staining is:
questions.explain: Safranin colours decolourized gram-negative cells pink.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Acid-fast staining (Ziehl–Neelsen) is used for:
questions.explain: Mycolic acid in the cell wall retains carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Spore staining commonly uses:
questions.explain: Schaeffer–Fulton method: malachite green with heat, safranin counterstain.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: India ink (negative staining) is used to demonstrate the capsule of:
questions.explain: The capsule appears as a clear halo against the dark background.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Endospores are formed by:
questions.explain: Bacillus (aerobic) and Clostridium (anaerobic) form heat-resistant endospores.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Bacteria lacking a cell wall are:
questions.explain: Mycoplasma have no cell wall, so penicillins do not act on them.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The phase of bacterial growth with maximum rate of division is:
questions.explain: Cells divide at a constant, maximal rate in log phase.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Bacteria that grow best at 20–45 °C are called:
questions.explain: Most human pathogens are mesophiles (optimum ~37 °C).

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Organisms that cannot tolerate oxygen are:
questions.explain: Oxygen is toxic to obligate anaerobes like Clostridium.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: A medium that allows growth of certain organisms while inhibiting others is:
questions.explain: E.g. MacConkey's bile salts inhibit gram-positives.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: MacConkey agar differentiates bacteria on the basis of:
questions.explain: Lactose fermenters form pink colonies.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Blood agar is used to observe:
questions.explain: α, β and γ hemolysis help identify streptococci.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Solidifying agent in culture media is:
questions.explain: Agar (from seaweed) melts ~85 °C and sets ~40 °C, and most microbes cannot digest it.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Viruses are:
questions.explain: Viruses replicate only inside living host cells.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Bacteriophages infect:
questions.explain: Phages are viruses that attack bacteria.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Fungal cell membrane contains:
questions.explain: Ergosterol is the target of azoles and amphotericin B.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Yeast reproduces asexually mainly by:
questions.explain: Saccharomyces reproduces by budding.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Sterility testing methods in the pharmacopoeia include:
questions.explain: Sterility test: membrane filtration or direct inoculation into media.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Fluid thioglycollate medium in sterility testing detects:
questions.explain: Thioglycollate supports anaerobes (and aerobes); soybean–casein digest is for fungi and aerobes.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Soybean–casein digest medium in sterility testing is incubated at:
questions.explain: SCDM at 20–25 °C (fungi, aerobes); thioglycollate at 30–35 °C.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Chemical indicator tape that changes colour after autoclaving shows that:
questions.correct: The item was exposed to sterilizing conditions (not proof of sterility)
questions.explain: Indicator tapes confirm exposure only; biological indicators prove lethality.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Biological indicator for dry heat and ethylene oxide sterilization is:
questions.explain: B. atrophaeus spores are used for dry heat and EtO.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Bacillus pumilus spores are used to validate:
questions.explain: B. pumilus is resistant to ionizing radiation.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Membrane filters used for sterilization have pore size:
questions.explain: 0.22 µm (or 0.2) filters retain bacteria.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Phenol coefficient test (Rideal–Walker) compares a disinfectant with phenol against:
questions.explain: R-W test uses S. typhi; Chick–Martin adds organic matter.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: The D-value in sterilization is the time needed to kill:
questions.explain: D-value = time at a given temperature for a 1-log (90%) reduction.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Tyndallization involves:
questions.correct: Steaming at 100 °C on three successive days
questions.explain: Intermittent steaming lets spores germinate between heatings.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Microbiological assay of antibiotics by cylinder-plate method measures:
questions.explain: The diameter of the inhibition zone relates to potency.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Which microbe is the test organism in the microbial assay of penicillin (cylinder-plate)?
questions.explain: Penicillin potency is assayed against a sensitive S. aureus strain.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Laminar air flow benches use ____ filters.
questions.explain: HEPA filters remove ≥99.97% of 0.3 µm particles.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: ISO Class 5 clean area corresponds roughly to old:
questions.explain: Class 100 = ≤100 particles ≥0.5 µm per cubic foot.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Lysozyme acts by breaking:
questions.correct: β-1,4 linkage between NAM and NAG in peptidoglycan
questions.explain: Lysozyme hydrolyses the glycan backbone of the cell wall.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Cell wall of gram-negative bacteria contains an outer membrane with:
questions.explain: LPS (endotoxin) is in the outer membrane; teichoic acids are in gram-positives.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Flagella arranged all over the bacterial surface are called:
questions.explain: Peritrichous flagella, e.g. E. coli and Salmonella.

questions.subject: micro
questions.q: Counting viable bacteria as colonies grown on agar plates is called:
questions.explain: Standard plate count gives colony-forming units, i.e. living cells only.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Flow is laminar in a pipe when Reynolds number is below about:
questions.explain: Re < 2000 laminar, 2000–4000 transitional, > 4000 turbulent.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Bernoulli's theorem is based on the principle of conservation of:
questions.explain: Total head (pressure + kinetic + potential) stays constant along a streamline.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Orifice meter and venturi meter measure:
questions.explain: Both use pressure drop across a constriction to find flow rate.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Rotameter is a:
questions.explain: The float rises in a tapered tube; area changes, pressure drop stays constant.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Manometers measure:
questions.explain: U-tube manometers read pressure difference from the liquid column height.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Ball mill works mainly on the principle of:
questions.explain: Falling balls give impact; rolling balls give attrition.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Critical speed of a ball mill is the speed at which:
questions.correct: Balls stick to the wall and no grinding occurs
questions.explain: Operate at about 65–75% of critical speed for best grinding.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Fluid energy mill (jet mill) is suitable for:
questions.correct: Very fine grinding of heat-sensitive drugs
questions.explain: Air jets cause particle collisions; expansion cools, so heat-labile drugs survive.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Hammer mill works on the principle of:
questions.explain: Rotating hammers strike particles at high speed.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Rittinger's law states that energy for size reduction is proportional to:
questions.explain: Rittinger: E ∝ (1/D2 − 1/D1), best for fine grinding.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Bond's law for size reduction says energy is proportional to:
questions.explain: Bond's law sits between Kick's (coarse) and Rittinger's (fine).

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Sieve number refers to:
questions.correct: Number of meshes per linear inch (or per 25.4 mm)
questions.explain: Higher sieve number = finer openings.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Andreasen pipette is used to determine:
questions.explain: It samples a settling suspension; Stokes' law gives particle size.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Stokes' law gives the:
questions.correct: Settling velocity of particles in a fluid
questions.explain: v = d²(ρs − ρ)g / 18η.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Heat transfer by direct molecular contact in solids is:
questions.explain: Conduction follows Fourier's law.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Thermal conductivity is highest for:
questions.explain: Metals like copper conduct heat far better than glass, water or air.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Stefan–Boltzmann law deals with heat transfer by:
questions.explain: Radiant energy ∝ T⁴ (absolute temperature).

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: A perfect black body has emissivity equal to:
questions.explain: A black body absorbs and emits all radiation; emissivity = 1.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Fick's law is related to:
questions.explain: Rate of diffusion ∝ concentration gradient.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Evaporator commonly used for heat-sensitive, foaming liquids is:
questions.explain: Film evaporators give a very short contact time.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Moisture content that remains in a solid at equilibrium with surrounding air is:
questions.explain: Below EMC no further drying is possible at that humidity.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: In the drying rate curve, the constant rate period ends at the:
questions.explain: After critical moisture, the falling rate period begins.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Spray dryer is preferred for:
questions.explain: Fine droplets dry in seconds, giving free-flowing spherical particles.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Fluidized bed dryer works best when the airflow:
questions.explain: Hot air lifts granules, giving rapid, uniform drying.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Freeze drying removes water by:
questions.explain: Ice goes directly to vapour under vacuum.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Fractional distillation is used to separate liquids whose boiling points:
questions.explain: The column gives many vaporization–condensation cycles.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Steam distillation is used for:
questions.explain: It lowers distillation temperature for heat-sensitive volatile oils.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Vacuum (reduced pressure) distillation is used for:
questions.explain: Lower pressure lowers the boiling point.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Darcy's law is the basis of:
questions.explain: Flow rate through a porous bed ∝ pressure drop and permeability.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: A filter aid commonly used is:
questions.explain: Diatomite forms a porous, incompressible cake.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Centrifugation separates particles based on:
questions.explain: Centrifugal force accelerates sedimentation.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Supersaturation is necessary for:
questions.explain: Miers' theory: nucleation and growth need supersaturation.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Miers' theory relates to:
questions.explain: Miers described solubility/supersolubility curves.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Mixer used for dry powders by tumbling is:
questions.explain: Tumbling mixers suit free-flowing powders.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Sigma-blade mixer is mainly used for:
questions.explain: Heavy blades knead cohesive masses.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Silverson mixer–homogenizer works on:
questions.explain: Rotor–stator high shear for emulsions and suspensions.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Corrosion is mainly an ____ process.
questions.explain: Anodic and cathodic reactions occur on the metal surface.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Stainless steel resists corrosion mainly because of:
questions.correct: Chromium forming a passive oxide layer
questions.explain: ≥10.5% chromium forms a protective Cr2O3 film.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Cathodic protection against corrosion uses:
questions.correct: A sacrificial anode like zinc or magnesium
questions.explain: The more active metal corrodes instead of the structure.

questions.subject: engg
questions.q: Dimensionless number relating heat transfer by convection to conduction is:
questions.explain: Nu = hL/k.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Drug that is a non-selective β-blocker:
questions.explain: Propranolol blocks β1 and β2; atenolol, metoprolol and bisoprolol are β1-selective.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Antidote for paracetamol poisoning is:
questions.explain: NAC replenishes glutathione to detoxify NAPQI.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Antidote for opioid overdose is:
questions.explain: Naloxone is a competitive opioid receptor antagonist.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Antidote for benzodiazepine overdose is:
questions.explain: Flumazenil antagonizes the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Antidote for heparin overdose is:
questions.explain: Protamine (basic) neutralizes acidic heparin.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Antidote for warfarin overdose is:
questions.explain: Vitamin K restores synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Organophosphate poisoning is treated with atropine and:
questions.explain: Pralidoxime reactivates phosphorylated acetylcholinesterase if given early.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits:
questions.explain: Aspirin acetylates COX; platelets cannot make new enzyme.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Drug of choice for anaphylactic shock is:
questions.explain: IM adrenaline reverses bronchospasm and hypotension.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Bioavailability of a drug given intravenously is:
questions.explain: IV dosing places the whole dose into systemic circulation.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: First-pass metabolism mainly occurs in the:
questions.explain: Oral drugs pass through the portal circulation to the liver before reaching the system.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Half-life of a drug following first-order kinetics:

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: A drug following zero-order kinetics at high doses is:
questions.explain: Phenytoin, ethanol and high-dose aspirin show saturation (zero-order) kinetics.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Number of half-lives needed to reach about 97% of steady state:

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Maintenance dose depends mainly on:
questions.explain: Maintenance dose rate = target concentration × CL / F.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Therapeutic index is the ratio of:

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: A drug with a narrow therapeutic index is:
questions.explain: Digoxin, lithium and warfarin need careful monitoring.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: An agonist that produces less than maximal response even at full receptor occupancy is a:
questions.explain: E.g. buprenorphine at μ-opioid receptors.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Competitive antagonism shifts the agonist dose-response curve:

questions.subject: pharmacology

questions.explain: The insulin receptor has intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity.

questions.subject: pharmacology

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Steroid hormones act via:
questions.explain: They regulate gene transcription.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Atropine is a:
questions.explain: Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors, causing dry mouth, tachycardia and mydriasis.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Neostigmine is used in:
questions.explain: It inhibits cholinesterase, increasing ACh at the neuromuscular junction.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Salbutamol is a:
questions.explain: It relaxes bronchial smooth muscle in asthma.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Drug of choice in type 2 diabetes (first line) is usually:
questions.explain: Metformin lowers hepatic glucose output and rarely causes hypoglycaemia.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Penicillins act by inhibiting:
questions.explain: β-lactams block transpeptidase (PBPs) in peptidoglycan cross-linking.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Fluoroquinolones like ciprofloxacin inhibit:
questions.explain: They block bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Tetracyclines inhibit protein synthesis by binding to:
questions.explain: They prevent aminoacyl-tRNA attachment at the 30S subunit.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Macrolides such as erythromycin bind to:
questions.explain: They block translocation at the 50S subunit.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Sulfonamides act by inhibiting:
questions.explain: They compete with PABA; trimethoprim inhibits DHFR.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Rifampicin inhibits:
questions.explain: Rifampicin also turns urine and tears orange-red.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Isoniazid mainly inhibits synthesis of:
questions.explain: INH blocks mycolic acid synthesis in mycobacteria.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Peripheral neuropathy due to isoniazid is prevented with:
questions.explain: INH increases pyridoxine excretion.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Omeprazole acts by inhibiting:
questions.explain: PPIs irreversibly block the final step of acid secretion.

questions.subject: pharmacology
questions.q: Ranitidine/famotidine are:
questions.explain: They block histamine H2 receptors on parietal cells.

questions.subject: pharmacology
